title: Fair Value Assessment
summary: How to assess whether the price consumers pay is reasonable relative to the benefits, costs and quality they receive, and how to challenge firms' value assessments.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to assess whether the price consumers pay is reasonable relative to the benefits, costs and quality they receive, and how to challenge firms' value assessments.
Learning Objectives: Apply a fair value framework to a financial product
Challenge the evidence behind a firm's value assessment
Identify pricing practices that cause foreseeable harm
Syllabus: Price, benefits, costs and quality as value components
Price walking, cross-subsidy and hidden charges
Value across distribution chains and add-on products
Exercise: testing a firm's fair value assessment
Intended Audience: Conduct and consumer protection supervisors and inspectors across all sectors
Policy staff working on consumer protection, disclosure or financial inclusion
Senior managers setting the authority's consumer protection priorities
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of conduct or consumer-facing supervision is helpful. No specialist background is required.
Core Reading: G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
World Bank, Good Practices for Financial Consumer Protection (2017)
CPMI and World Bank, Payment Aspects of Financial Inclusion (2016)
